title: Ohm’s law as a relation
description: V = I R ties push, flow, and squeeze together. Change one and the others must move.

blocks.md:
## Three letters, one relation

Ohm’s law says the push, the flow, and the squeeze belong together: V = I × R. If you know two, you can find the third. Cover V and you multiply. Cover I and you divide V by R. Cover R and you divide V by I. In this pack a cell is one unit of V, so I ≈ cells ÷ ohms.

This bites when you treat the ohms knob as a brightness control that ignores the battery, or when you memorize the triangle and forget what the letters mean on a loop.

![Ohm’s law triangle](assets/ohms-law.svg)

```text
V = I × R
I = V ÷ R
R = V ÷ I
```

A common mistake is changing R and expecting brightness to move while pretending V is not in the story. The questions ask you to compute I and to name the relation.

blocks.promptMd: V = 4 and R = 2. What is I?
To find current you compute {{a}}. To find voltage you compute {{b}}.
blocks.explainMd: I = V ÷ R. V = I × R. Same relation, different cover.

blocks.promptMd: Same 2 Ω resistor. What is I for each push?
blocks.explainMd: 2 ÷ 2 = 1. 4 ÷ 2 = 2. Double the push, double the current if R stays put.
